_outlets_note: The user's outlet map. 2026-10-04: 0 pi5, 1 pi4. 2026-10-05 14:03: 0 pi4, 1 pi5 (confirmed by load 14:27). 2026-10-05 ~17:45: the Pi 5 was returned and the user plugged the LAPTOP (ThinkPad T580, the control and prefill node) into outlet 1, renamed laptop on the strip at the same time. The laptop's figure is its charger at the wall: valid only while the battery reads fully-charged (energy-rate 0 W). 2026-10-08 ~18:10: the strip was factory reset while being joined to the home router's Wi-Fi (WIFI-A, now 192.168.1.111): names cleared and every outlet's initial_state back to off, so it powered the boards off until its buttons were pressed (~18:15). With the user's yes, initial_state is on again for all four outlets and the names are restored, outlet 3 as unused (testbed/energy/strip_config_20261008.json). Its setup AP was left on (not approved to change). 2026-10-19 ~23:30: the Pi 5 came back (a replacement board, the old SD card) and the plugs were moved: measured by load bursts (the Pi 4, the Pi 5, the laptop; the Jetson by elimination, idle 1.8 W) as 0 Pi 4, 1 Jetson, 2 Pi 5, 3 laptop (+ its USB-C hub). No run had used the strip since 10-11, so no recorded energy is affected. With the user's yes (~23:35) the strip's names were set to match (testbed/energy/strip_config_20261019.json; nothing switched). The map before is kept read-only as strip.20261019_before_pi5_back.json. Runs pass --outlets pi4=0,jetson=1,pi5=2,laptop=3.

auth_file_hint: auth is off on the strip (auth_en false, 2026-10-04). If a password is set, it goes in ~/.config/heteroserve/shelly.auth (chmod 600), never in the repo; pass --auth-file or set SHELLY_AUTH_FILE.
